podcast.title: Band's Disgruntlement and Departure
podcast.body: Following the poor performance of "Rock House," The Teen Kings became increasingly disgruntled, believing Sam Phillips didn't care about them and feeling Roy Orbison monopolized the spotlight. They secretly decided to leave, packing up their equipment and driving away during a scheduled recording session while Orbison and Phillips were on a break. "Rock House didn't do very well, and the band were getting this gruntled. They felt that some Phillips didn't care about any of them, and they were also getting a bit sick of Roy himself, who they thought was taking too much of the spotlight, so they secretly made an agreement."

podcast.title: Columbia Records Audition and Rejection
podcast.body: The Teen Kings auditioned for Columbia Records, recording "Ooby Dooby" and a cover of The Clovers' "Hey Miss Fanny." Columbia rejected them but liked "Ooby Dooby" enough to give it to Sid King and the Five Strings. "So instead the Team Kings went into the studio to audition for Columbia Records. They recorded two tracks at that initial session."

podcast.title: Local TV Series
podcast.body: The Teen Kings established their own local TV series, in addition to their radio shows, further enhancing their regional presence. "The Team Kings soon got their own local TV series to go with the local radio shows they already had."

podcast.title: Renamed from The Wink Westerners
podcast.body: This group was formerly known as The Wink Westerners and later signed to Sun Records with Roy Orbison as their singer. "who changed their name to the team Kings and were signed to Sun Records."
